decision: Locked a drowned nave called the Reliquary of the Last Sun, one amber key from the upper right, bone and tide, gouache via the sculpt brush
why: A shared palette and light let many files stay one picture. Separate files are how the agents avoid writing the same scene.
The file split is the one the language already uses, one def per file, and a bake-off would only restate it.

decision: Kept the material study even though the warden cluster is a clumsy silhouette
why: The slab shows the stone and the light. The creature drawings are the workers' job, judged against the bogmaw's density.

decision: Local workers, each in its own worktree, because cloud workers were not requested
why: Parallel builds would race on one art-manifest. A worktree gives each sprite its own assets directory.

decision: Saved the empty nave as timelapse frame 00
why: The later frames need a picture of the room before any sprite, so the fill-in is visible.

decision: Started nineteen sprite workers, one worktree each, on grok
why: Opus was refused for the six hero sprites because the other-model spend limit was reached, so those six were started again on the same worker model as the rest.

decision: Merged the ember field and left it out of the nave
why: The PNG is a sparse amber scatter with a few ash flakes, which is what the direction asked for. Placing it now would be dots on an empty room.

decision: Merged the salt ledge and left it out of the nave
why: The PNG reads as one bone platform, pale on the upper right, chipped at that corner, salt on the old lip. The walk surface is the def origin.

decision: Merged the cracked pier and moved its brush let inside the def
why: The column reads in shade, with a bite, salt, and the sole on the origin. A top-level let would vanish when the scene imports the def, so the brush binding now lives in the def. The PNG bytes did not change.
